acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Goblins family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Cutter, T2, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Scrap-Line Bully (Soldier) archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two normal construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: Adds a stolen helmet three sizes too big, mismatched leather scraps, a notched cleaver, and a small coin pouch while remaining hunched and visibly under-armored.

Signature mechanic: Bully's Hook: the Cutter catches clothing or guard with the notch in its cleaver and leans back, slowing the target while any adjacent Runt gains Mob Nerve from the protected position.
battlefieldDuty: Hold a messy front line by pinning one target in place while Runts crowd the exposed sides.
constructionDimensions: Material provenance stays mundane and legible: muddy rags, patched leather, cracked doors, frayed rope, rusted scrap, bone, coins, and stolen heraldry retain their original mismatched sources.

Surface and motion effects stay physical: grime, sweat, kicked dust, wobbling oversized gear, loose coins, and brief impact sparks emphasize weight and poor repair without adding supernatural residue.
counterplay: Sidestep the narrow hook, strike during the helmet-blind recovery, or push the Cutter away from its Runts to collapse both the pin and their Mob Nerve. Affinity signal: Readable hands, ropes, shield hinges, banner poles, loot chutes, and exposed carriers reveal the same physical weak points described by each form's mechanic.
forbiddenTreatments: Matching manufactured equipment that erases the scavenged construction language
identityInvariants: Short, hunched, long-armed humanoid silhouette with an oversized head and pointed ears, disproportionately large hands and feet, hooked nose, and crowded crooked teeth.
Sickly green or grey-green skin against muddy browns, rust-orange, dull iron, and sparse accents of stolen gold.
Every carried object reads as stolen, scavenged, or crudely repaired: rags, patched leather, cracked wood, rusted scrap metal, bone, and rope rather than purpose-built matching equipment.
Loot is the status language: mismatched helmets, coin necklaces, teeth, rings, captured banners, and trophies accumulate with rank.
Posture and finish communicate hierarchy, from a knock-kneed cringing crouch to an upright swagger amid increasingly prestigious plunder.
telegraph: It drops its oversized helmet over its eyes, turns the cleaver notch inward, and plants one foot before the hook.
